comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
═══ MEASURED: code-novelty is one of FOUR, and it is the SMALLEST of them. 18 of 23 calls in a plan
review go to direct Anthropic. ═══

Experiment run at the operator's request: configure all three model classes on **Bedrock**, leave
`cfg.model` at the bare direct-Anthropic default, then run every workflow end-to-end and read the
usage log. In that configuration the provider is the verdict — **bedrock** means the cfg reaching a
call was class-resolved (correct), **anthropic** means it inherited raw `cfg` (a bypass).

No new instrumentation was needed: `op` is `",".join(req.reviewers)`, and every hand-built sub-call
passes a distinctive reviewer id, so `op` identifies the site. **Zero calls failed in any run**
(checked stderr for every workflow), so no rows are missing and the counts below are complete — that
check matters because a failed call writes no row at all (ticket 8455).

    workflow            op                                    calls  provider   verdict
    ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    review-plan         overlap-judge                           18   anthropic  ** BYPASS **
    review-plan         ticket-digest                            1   anthropic  ** BYPASS **
    review-plan         plan-reviewer                            1   bedrock    ok
    review-plan         plan-review-prerequisite-verifier        1   bedrock    ok
    review-plan         plan-review-verifier                     1   bedrock    ok
    review-plan         plan-review-coach                        1   bedrock    ok
    review              ticket-quality                           1   anthropic  ** BYPASS **
    review-code         code-novelty                             1   anthropic  ** BYPASS **
    review-code         (7 workflow steps: base/overlays/verify/coach)  bedrock  ok
    verify-completion   completion-verifier                       1   bedrock    ok

**THE FOUR BYPASS SITES — one root cause, one fix shape:** a hand-built `RunRequest` that passes
`config=cfg` and declares no model class, so it inherits `cfg.model` regardless of configuration.

    llm/overlap/judge.py:46            op=overlap-judge    18 calls  <-- DOMINATES the gate's traffic
    llm/enrich.py:81                   op=ticket-digest     1 call   <-- runs on the STORE WRITE path
    llm/operations.py:177              op=ticket-quality    1 call
    llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:571 op=code-novelty     1 call   <-- what this ticket originally named

**WHY overlap-judge CHANGES THE SEVERITY OF THIS TICKET.** It is not a stray sub-call: it made 18 of
the 23 LLM calls in a plan review — the single largest consumer in the gate — and every one went to
direct Anthropic while everything else was on Bedrock. For an operator who has "cut over to Bedrock",
the *majority* of plan-review traffic never moved. That is a cost, a data-residency and a
correctness story at once, and it is invisible without the per-call attribution.

**`ticket-digest` IS THE MOST INSIDIOUS OF THE FOUR** because it is not in a gate at all:
`enrich_drain.maybe_drain` is called from `_store/event_append.py:609` and `_store/push.py:295`, so it
runs on the **ticket store write path** — the `enrich drain gate check took ~230ms` line that appears
on ordinary `rebar comment`/`create` calls. It therefore sends ticket content to direct Anthropic
during routine store operations, with no gate invocation and nothing in a verdict to reveal it.

**WHAT CORRECTLY HONOURS THE CONFIG** (so the fix does not need to touch it): all four plan-review
passes, the completion verifier, and all seven code-review workflow steps. Notably
`plan-review-prerequisite-verifier` resolved to Bedrock, i.e. `prerequisites.py:228`'s per-call
`call_cfg` is now honoured — that is story b690's fix working on a second, independent path.

**A PREDICTION I MADE THAT WAS WRONG, recorded so it is not repeated.** I expected `plan-reviewer` to
be ambiguous between `passes.py:319` and `prerequisites.py:228` because both pass
`reviewers=["plan-reviewer"]` in source. In the live log they are distinct ops
(`plan-reviewer` vs `plan-review-prerequisite-verifier`), so the reviewer id is set elsewhere on that
path and no disambiguating instrumentation was needed after all.

**NOT YET EXERCISED, stated rather than assumed clean:** `spec_scan.py:123` (needs a `--spec-file`),
and the two eval-harness sites (`evals/eval_solver.py`, `plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py`) which do
not run in a production sweep. `overlap_enabled` turned out to be ON in this repo's config — I had
assumed it defaulted off, and the measurement corrected me.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
═══ CONFIG A (everything on Bedrock, INCLUDING cfg.model): 15 calls, ZERO on Anthropic — but the
headline number overstates the coverage, so here is what it does and does not establish. ═══

Second half of the operator's experiment. Config B (classes Bedrock, `cfg.model` left bare-anthropic)
found the four bypass sites. Config A additionally points `cfg.model` at Bedrock, so a call that
merely INHERITS cfg now lands on Bedrock too. The two configurations answer different questions:

* **Config B** — does every call honour the CLASS configuration? (found 4 that do not)
* **Config A** — is any provider HARDCODED past configuration entirely? (found none)

Config A alone is necessary but NOT sufficient: it would have passed even with every bypass site
unfixed, because a bypassing call inherits `cfg.model` and `cfg.model` is Bedrock. Anyone re-running
this later should run BOTH, or the result is a false clean.

    workflow            calls   non-bedrock
    review-plan            5         0
    verify-completion      1         0
    review                 1         0
    review-code            8         0
    ─────────────────────────────────────
    TOTAL                 15         0        (and 0 FAILED calls in every run, so no rows are missing)

**THREE OF THE FOUR BYPASS SITES WERE EXERCISED AND ALL WENT TO BEDROCK** — `ticket-digest`,
`ticket-quality`, `code-novelty`. That is real evidence for the mechanism: they inherit `cfg.model`,
so moving `cfg.model` moves them.

**THE FOURTH, `overlap-judge`, DID NOT RUN IN CONFIG A — its zero is ABSENCE, NOT CORRECTNESS.**
Recording this rather than letting the total imply coverage it does not have. Two probes tried to
force it and both failed to, which is itself the useful finding:
 * re-running `review-plan` on 03b0 (the ticket that produced 18 overlap calls in config B) made
   **zero LLM calls of any kind** — a current attestation short-circuits the whole gate.
 * running `review-plan` on 00da, never reviewed before, made 5 calls and still no overlap-judge.

**SETTLED FROM THE CODE INSTEAD, which is conclusive here.** `overlap/judge.py:judge_one` builds
`RunRequest(config=cfg, reviewers=["overlap-judge"], ...)` — raw `cfg`, no class — and
`wire.py:overlap_findings` sets `cfg = config or LLMConfig.from_env(...)`. That is the IDENTICAL
mechanism measured three times over in config A, so under `cfg.model = bedrock` it resolves to
Bedrock, and under a class-only Bedrock config it does not (which is exactly the 18 anthropic calls
config B measured). No further run is needed to characterise it.

**AND THE TRIGGER IS NOW KNOWN, for whoever writes the regression test.** `wire.py` runs the judge
only when BM25F retrieval returns candidates: `candidates = retrieve(...)` then
`if not candidates: return []`. Candidates exclude the query's own graph
(`graph.related_ticket_ids`). So the 18 calls happened because 03b0 had many unrelated-but-similar
neighbours at that moment; afeb and 00da had none. **A test for this must construct the candidate
condition deliberately — it cannot rely on running a gate and hoping the judge fires.**

**WHAT CONFIG A PROVES, stated exactly:** no provider is hardcoded past configuration in
review-plan, review, review-code or verify-completion. Combined with config B, the complete claim is:
"every call reaches Bedrock when everything is configured for Bedrock, but four of them get there by
inheriting `cfg` rather than by honouring the class — so a class-only cutover still leaks."

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
═══ OPERATOR DESIGN RULE — this decides the class each bypass site must select ═══

From the operator, recorded as a standing decision so the implementer does not have to guess:

**For REVIEWS, Pass-2 and Pass-4 are DESIGNED to use a sonnet-equivalent model (the `standard`
class), with LIMITED ESCAPE HATCHES for escalation to a higher class (`frontier`).**

Consequences for this ticket:
* the fix is NOT "give these calls `frontier`" — the default for verification/judging work is
  `standard`. A site that needs frontier must justify it as an explicit, bounded escape hatch, not
  as its normal path.
* `code-novelty` is Pass-2-adjacent verification, so `standard` — which also RESOLVES the docstring
  parity question on this ticket: plan-review's novelty sub-call uses `_verifier_cfg` (the verifier
  model), and under this rule the two agree rather than diverge.
* `overlap-judge` is a narrow pairwise judgement, the same shape of work, so `standard` unless there
  is a measured reason otherwise. Note it is the VOLUME site (18 of 23 calls in a plan review), so
  putting it on frontier would be the most expensive possible reading of this ticket.
* `ticket-digest` and `ticket-quality` are small extraction/scoring tasks, not open-ended reasoning;
  `standard` is the conservative default and `trivial` is worth considering on measurement.

It also settles a question left open on story b690: making `_verifier_cfg` effective moved three
plan-review Pass-2 sub-calls from frontier onto the verifier model. **That is the DESIGNED behaviour,
not a regression** — b690 did not change any intent, it made the existing intent take effect.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
═══ FIX LANDED IN WORKTREE (branch fix/afeb-class-bypass) — four sites now select from the class
vocabulary, plus a GENERAL provenance guard so a fifth cannot appear silently ═══

**RED first, confirmed.** New file `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`. Before any source
change all six per-site probes failed with the discriminating string, e.g.
`assert 'anthropic:cfg-model-must-not-be-inherited' == 'test:standard-class-model'` — i.e. the site
ran cfg.model while a class table was configured. That is exactly the ticket's config B, expressed
offline: the class table is patched at `llm.config._read_llm_file_table` (the one function
`load_class_slots` reads) with all three classes pointed at sentinels DISTINCT from cfg.model, so
"honoured the class" and "fell through to cfg.model" are different strings rather than the same one.

**MUTATION CHECK (the test has teeth).** With the fix in place I re-introduced the exact root cause
at all four sites (replaced each binding with `pass`) and re-ran: 8 tests returned to RED — the six
probes and both guards. Restored, 12/12 green.

**THE FOUR CLASS CHOICES, each decided on the PROMPT's shape (execution_mode + tools +
open-endedness), not on "it's a sub-call". This reasoning is the durable part and is written into
each site as a comment:**

    site                                  class      why
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    llm/enrich.py (ticket-digest)         trivial    single_turn, NO tools, "Not a reviewer";
                                                     extracts four constrained fields from given
                                                     text. Narrow canonicalizing work — and the
                                                     highest-VOLUME site (store write path), so the
                                                     cheapest win of the four.
    llm/overlap/judge.py (overlap-judge)  standard   single_turn, tool-less, but picks ONE relation
                                                     from a closed 5-value set and must cite a named
                                                     shared artifact while "false flags are costly".
                                                     Precision-sensitive JUDGEMENT = the operator's
                                                     default. NOT frontier: 18 of 23 calls.
    code_review/workflow_ops.py           standard   IS a code-review pass (category
      (code-novelty)                                 `code-review-pass`, factual tri-state match), so
                                                     the Pass-2/Pass-4 rule applies directly. This
                                                     also makes the docstring's claimed parity with
                                                     plan-review's `_score_floor_novelty` (which runs
                                                     `_verifier_cfg` = standard) TRUE; it was false.
    llm/operations.py (ticket-quality)    frontier   NOT standard. This is `rebar review`'s default
                                                     reviewer: `execution_mode: agentic`, category
                                                     `review`, WITH file + MCP tools, told to inspect
                                                     the code paths a ticket references. An
                                                     open-ended FINDER (Pass-1 analogue); the
                                                     standard rule covers verification passes.

Fix shape at every site: `cfg = replace(cfg, model=resolve_model_string(<CLASS>))`, the same
mechanism `_verifier_cfg` and the completion verifier already use. Placed INSIDE the existing
try/except at the two fail-safe sites, so a config error is still an abstain (overlap stays advisory
and never blocks) / still yields `{}` (novelty degrades to keeping MORE findings). Both fail-safes
have their own tests in the new file.

`ticket-digest` is bound INSIDE `enrich()` rather than at its callers, deliberately: the store write
path (`enrich_drain.drain` → `enrich`) builds its own config from the environment and passes none in,
so a caller-side fix would have missed exactly the path that matters most. There is a probe for that
`config=None` route.

**THE GENERAL GUARD — a provenance analysis, not a list of today's four.**
`test_no_run_request_inherits_the_raw_config_model` walks the AST of every `.py` in `src/rebar`,
finds every `RunRequest(...)`, and traces its `config=` expression backwards: a class binder
(`resolve_model_string`/`resolve_model`/`_verifier_cfg`/…) anywhere in the chain cleanses it, a bare
`LLMConfig.from_env` at the end of it is the defect, and a PARAMETER transfers the obligation to
that function's callers across the whole package (which is how it reaches `judge_one` through
`judge()`). Verdicts are bound / raw / unresolved. Pre-fix it reported
`enrich`, `review_ticket`, `judge_one` as raw and `score_code_novelty` as an unregistered
unfollowable site — i.e. it flagged all four WITHOUT naming any of them.

Two small registries carry the sites the rule cannot pass on its own, each entry with a written
reason, and both are staleness-checked so an entry cannot rot into a licence:
 * `_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN` — exactly ONE entry: `spec_scan._scan_epics_inner`. It is a top-level op's
   PRIMARY call (not a sub-call), and it is the one site the ticket's measurement could not exercise
   (needs `--spec-file`), so afeb scopes it out rather than change it unmeasured. **Flagging this
   for the operator**: if `scan-spec` should also move onto the class vocabulary, that is a separate
   one-line change — I did not make it, both because it is out of this ticket's measured scope and
   because `src/rebar/llm/spec_scan.py` was outside my file budget for this parallel run.
 * `_UNFOLLOWABLE` — 7 entries the analysis stops at (attribute configs like
   `completion_recovery`'s `self._config`; params whose binding happens through call chains it does
   not follow: `passes.pass1_chunk`, `passes.pass4_coach`, `prerequisites.run_focused_finder`; and
   three eval harnesses that pin cfg.model as their control).

Also asserted: the scan itself finds ≥15 sites and every site passes SOME config, so the guard
cannot pass vacuously if `RunRequest` construction ever moves behind a factory.

**One deliberate weakening of the analysis, recorded rather than hidden**: when a name has several
assignments, `bound` wins over `raw`. That is required for the rebind shape the fix itself uses
(`cfg = replace(cfg, model=resolve_model_string(...))`) and for the workflow engine's own
`RunnerAgentStep`, which mints from `from_env` then rebinds via `resolve_model`. The cost: a function
that binds a class for one call and passes the raw config to a SECOND RunRequest would read as bound.
The per-site probes cover the places where that would currently matter.

Gates: `make lint` clean, `make typecheck` clean (mypy, 407 files). All four touched src files stay
well under the 800-line cap (largest: workflow_ops.py at 691). Targeted suites green: the new file,
enrich/enrich_drain/enrich_queue/overlap_judge/overlap_retrieve/plan_review_overlap/
ticket_digest_store/model_classes (128 passed, 1 skipped), and tests/unit/workflow +
code_review region-gate/per-pass-classes/verifier-class (539 passed).

**NOT done / for the reviewer:** `docs/env-vars.md` was not regenerated (no env-var surface changed).
`llm/overlap/wire.py` needed no change — binding inside `judge_one` covers every route into it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
═══ AN INCONSISTENCY IN THE SHIPPED FIX, and I think it is MY class-assignment guidance that is wrong,
not the implementation. Raising rather than quietly reverting. ═══

The implementation left `spec_scan._scan_epics_inner` on raw `cfg.model`, registered as
`_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN`, with this reason: **it is a TOP-LEVEL OP'S PRIMARY CALL**, not a sub-call
within a multi-pass gate. I think that reasoning is correct.

But by exactly the same reasoning, **`operations.py:177` (`review_ticket`, op=`ticket-quality`) is also a
top-level op's primary call** — it is the single LLM call of `rebar review`, and its prompt is
`default: true` for that operation. It was moved to `frontier` on my instruction. So the change treats
two structurally identical sites differently.

**WHY I NOW THINK `frontier` WAS THE WRONG CALL THERE.** I classified it by prompt shape — agentic,
file + MCP tools, open-ended — which correctly says "this is a finder, not a verification pass". That
reasoning is sound for choosing BETWEEN classes. What it misses is whether the class vocabulary should
apply AT ALL. The class vocabulary exists so a MULTI-PASS gate can spend differently per pass — "cheap
here, smart there". `rebar review` is a SINGLE call: there is no "here versus there" to differentiate,
so `cfg.model` is the operator's legitimate knob for it, exactly as for `spec_scan`.

**AND IT HAS A CONCRETE COST, which the implementer flagged:** an operator who steers by setting the
bare `llm.model` CONFIG-FILE key no longer steers `rebar review` at all — it is pinned to whatever
`frontier` resolves to (opus by default). That REMOVES single-knob operator control and hardcodes a
class, which is the opposite of what epic 061c exists to do. (The deprecated `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` env is
unaffected, since d23e fans it out into every class slot — so the surprise lands specifically on
config-file users, the non-deprecated path.)

**RECOMMENDATION:** revert `operations.py` to raw `cfg.model` and register it as
`_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN` alongside `spec_scan`, with the reason stated as "top-level op's primary call —
`cfg.model` IS the knob; the class vocabulary is for per-pass differentiation inside a gate". That
leaves the fix covering the three genuine sub-calls (`ticket-digest` → trivial, `overlap-judge` →
standard, `code-novelty` → standard), which is where the bypass actually was, and makes the general
AST guard's two design-exemptions consistent with each other rather than arbitrary.

Flagging for the operator rather than acting, because it reverses guidance I gave explicitly and
because `frontier` for a finder is a defensible reading of their Pass-1/Pass-2 rule — the question is
whether a single-call op has passes at all. Change 1194 carries the current version.

Separately, the implementer's general guard is worth noting as the durable asset here: an AST
provenance analysis over EVERY `RunRequest` in `src/rebar` that traces the `config=` expression
backwards, treating a parameter as transferring the obligation to that function's callers. It flagged
all four sites pre-fix WITHOUT naming them, which is what the ticket's "general defect" criterion
asked for and what stops a future hand-built sub-call from silently reintroducing this.

DISAMBIGUATION — two earlier comments on this ticket reference a bare 4-char id `00da`, which is AMBIGUOUS in this store and makes the resolver error during close-path text scans:

  00da-1bda-d59c-4c2e  in_progress  rebar comment silently stores a flag-looking argument as the body
  00da-b1af-89d4-4c47  closed       IR-to-BPMN serializer and rebar moddle extension

Both prior references mean **00da-1bda-d59c-4c2e** (the `rebar comment` body-handling bug). Context
confirms it: the sentences concern running `review-plan` on a never-reviewed ticket and overlap-judge
candidate neighbours during this epic's work, which is that ticket, not the BPMN serializer.

The two comments cannot be edited (events are append-only), so this comment is the disambiguation of
record.

compiled_state.description:
# Hand-built LLM sub-calls bypass the model-class config and go to direct Anthropic

## Scope: FOUR sites, one root cause, THREE take the class fix

Each builds a `RunRequest` by hand with `config=cfg` and declares no model class, so it inherits
`cfg.model` regardless of how the three model classes are configured. MEASURED, not inferred — see
the comments for the full experiment:

    llm/overlap/judge.py:46              op=overlap-judge    18 calls   <-- 18 of 23 in a plan review
    llm/enrich.py:81                     op=ticket-digest     1 call    <-- runs on the STORE WRITE path
    llm/operations.py:177                op=ticket-quality    1 call
    llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:571  op=code-novelty      1 call    <-- the site originally filed

Everything else honours the configuration: all four plan-review passes, the completion verifier, and
all seven code-review workflow steps.

## Why this matters beyond consistency

Bedrock is normally chosen for data-residency, procurement or contractual reasons. These calls send
real content to direct Anthropic: the diff and prior findings (`code-novelty`), ticket text
(`ticket-digest`, `ticket-quality`), and ticket digests for pairwise comparison (`overlap-judge`).

**`overlap-judge` dominates plan-review traffic** — 18 of 23 calls. An operator who cuts over by
configuring the three classes (the documented mechanism, and the one story eb6e will use) leaves the
MAJORITY of plan-review traffic on direct Anthropic.

**`ticket-digest` is the most insidious** because it is not in a gate at all: `enrich_drain.maybe_drain`
is called from `_store/event_append.py:609` and `_store/push.py:295`, so it runs on the ticket STORE
WRITE path — on ordinary `rebar comment` / `rebar create` calls, with no gate invocation and nothing
in any verdict to reveal it.

## The two configurations, and why both are needed

* classes on Bedrock, `cfg.model` left bare-anthropic → PRE-FIX, all four sites above show `anthropic`: they
  bypass the class config. This is the defect.
* classes AND `cfg.model` on Bedrock → 15 calls, 0 on anthropic: nothing is HARDCODED past config.

The second configuration passes even with this bug unfixed, because a bypassing call inherits
`cfg.model`. Any regression test must therefore pin the FIRST configuration, or it proves nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] with a model-class table configured to values that DIFFER from `cfg.model`, no hand-built
      SUB-CALL in review-plan, review-code or verify-completion resolves to `cfg.model` — verified
      IN-SESSION by `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`, which configures exactly such a
      table (the only configuration in which "honoured the class" and "fell through to cfg.model"
      are distinguishable strings — with no table configured both resolve to the same default and
      the observation carries no information) and asserts, per site, the model that reaches the
      runner. The two TOP-LEVEL one-call ops (`operations.py::review_ticket`,
      `spec_scan.py::_scan_epics_inner`) are EXCLUDED by design and registered in
      `_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN`. Reframed from "asserted from a live run's usage log": the property is
      a durable invariant of the code, so it belongs in a test that fails the day a new bypassing
      sub-call is written, not in a one-off credentialed run that cannot be re-checked.
- [ ] each of the THREE hand-built sub-call sites selects its model from the class
      vocabulary, and the class chosen for each is stated in the code with its reason rather
      than left implicit: `enrich.py` (ticket-digest) -> trivial, `overlap/judge.py`
      (overlap-judge) -> standard, `code_review/workflow_ops.py::score_code_novelty`
      (code-novelty) -> standard. The fourth site originally in scope,
      `operations.py::review_ticket`, is DELIBERATELY left on `cfg.model` and registered in
      `_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN` with that reason: it is a top-level op's single LLM call, so
      there are no passes to differentiate and the operator's configured model is the right
      knob. Narrowed from "four sites" after the operator decision that one-call top-level
      ops keep `cfg.model`; the code was already correct and the criterion was stale.
- [ ] `code-novelty`'s choice is consistent with plan-review's novelty sub-call, or the difference is
      documented as deliberate at both sites — `score_code_novelty`'s docstring currently claims it
      "mirrors" `_score_floor_novelty`, which uses `_verifier_cfg`, and that parity does not hold
- [ ] a test fails if ANY hand-built sub-call inherits `cfg.model` while a class table is configured
      — the general defect, so a future hand-built sub-call cannot silently reintroduce it. A test
      that enumerates today's four sites by name does NOT satisfy this
